hot.title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind
hot.summary: The Orca project by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence proposes "Next-State-Prediction" as a unified paradigm for general world foundation models, learning a latent world representation from multimodal data through both unconscious and conscious learning. The model demonstrates scalable learning behavior and improved performance in text generation, physically plausible image prediction, and emergent action generation across diverse downstream tasks with a frozen backbone.

hot.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
hot.summary: A speculative decoding framework named DSpark integrates semi-autoregressive generation with confidence-scheduled verification to enhance Large Language Model inference efficiency. It significantly improves per-user generation speeds and aggregate throughput in live production environments by dynamically optimizing draft quality and resource allocation.

hot.title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters: Reaching Trillion-Parameter Performance with a 35B Agent
hot.summary: The Agents-A1 project by Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory introduces a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that attains performance levels comparable to trillion-parameter models on long-horizon tasks by emphasizing agentic horizon scaling. The model notably outperformed 1T-parameter models on benchmarks like SEAL-0 (56.4) and IFBench (80.6) and demonstrated gold-medal-level results in a 12-hour machine learning optimization task.

hot.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
hot.summary: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) is a post-training paradigm that integrates multiple specialized capabilities, such as mathematical reasoning and instruction following, into a single Large Language Model. The method uses on-policy distillation with prompt-routed domain teachers to overcome issues like exposure bias and cross-domain interference. It achieved a normalized score of 0.9373 on Qwen3-30B-A3B and scaled effectively to a 309B-parameter industrial model.

hot.title: DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation
hot.summary: Dual On-policy Distillation (DOPD) introduces an adaptive, dual distillation strategy to transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, mitigating the "privilege illusion" observed when privileged information is used. The framework improved distillation efficiency, leading to an average 12.3-point gain for LLMs and 10.1-point gain for VLMs on challenging benchmarks.

hot.title: ScaleAware-JEPA: Latent Representation for Discovery in Multiscale Physical Fields
hot.summary: The ScaleAware-JEPA framework constructs dense, label-free latent representations for continuous scalar fields by explicitly integrating multiscale organization into self-supervised learning. Applying this method to diverse physical fields like MHD turbulence and galactic molecular gas reveals coherent structural atlases, enabling data-driven discovery without predefined labels.

hot.title: AdaJEPA: An Adaptive Latent World Model
hot.summary: AdaJEPA introduces an adaptive latent world model that continuously recalibrates its predictions during deployment, improving planning success for goal-conditioned control under visual and dynamics distribution shifts. This approach significantly boosts performance, such as doubling success rates on unseen object shapes, while incurring minimal computational overhead.

hot.title: Xiaomi-GUI-0 Technical Report
hot.summary: Xiaomi-GUI-0, developed by the SeerRay Team, introduces an end-to-end multimodal GUI agent for real mobile environments, utilizing a real-device closed-loop training and evaluation paradigm. The 30-billion-parameter model achieves a 72.0% success rate on the new RealMobile benchmark and 78.9% on AndroidWorld, demonstrating robust performance in complex reasoning and planning.

hot.title: TRIAGE: Role-Typed Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: TRIAGE is a framework that refines credit assignment in agentic reinforcement learning by introducing a four-role semantic taxonomy and an LLM-based judge to provide segment-level process rewards, addressing the limitations of sparse, outcome-only feedback. The method consistently improved success rates across ALFWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop benchmarks by up to 18.4% and reduced rollout length in completed tasks by over 10%.

hot.title: GR2 Technical Report
hot.summary: GR2, a generative reasoning re-ranker developed by Meta AI, integrates Large Language Models into the re-ranking stage of industrial recommendation systems, achieving +18.7% Recall@1 and approximately 15x serving-ROI improvement over legacy baselines.

hot.title: SWE-Together: Evaluating Coding Agents in Interactive User Sessions
hot.summary: SWE-Together is a new benchmark for evaluating coding agents using 109 repository-level tasks derived from real, multi-turn user-agent coding sessions, alongside an anchored, state-conditional LLM user simulator. The benchmark quantifies both final code correctness and interaction quality, revealing that stronger models, such as Claude Opus 4.8 (63% pass@1), require less corrective user intervention (1.38 mean User Correction score).

hot.title: ShopX: A Foundation Model for Intent-to-Item Fulfillment in Agentic Shopping
hot.summary: ShopX, a foundation model developed by Alibaba Taobao & Tmall Group, unifies intent understanding and item fulfillment for agentic shopping by directly translating natural language into catalog-grounded outcomes. The model achieved improved performance on multi-turn, stateful tasks, outperforming tool-mediated LLM-agent baselines in metrics like item precision and feedback adaptation.

hot.title: OSWorld2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
hot.summary: OSWORLD 2.0 introduces a new benchmark for computer-use agents, featuring 108 long-horizon, multi-application tasks grounded in real-world scenarios. Evaluations using this benchmark reveal that frontier agents achieve only 20.6% task completion, highlighting limitations in sustained planning, state management, and error recovery compared to previous benchmarks.

hot.title: Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning
hot.summary: WORLDEVOLVER introduces a self-evolving world model framework for LLM agents that improves predictive accuracy and planning success by dynamically updating external episodic and semantic memories, without requiring parameter updates to the base LLM. The framework yields an average improvement in agent success rates by +2.24 points on ALFWorld and +3.33 points on ScienceWorld for the Gemma-4-26B-A4B backbone by employing selective, confidence-gated foresight.

hot.title: Autodata: An agentic data scientist to create high quality synthetic data
hot.summary: Autodata introduces an agentic framework for autonomously generating and curating high-quality synthetic data to train large language models (LLMs). Through iterative feedback and meta-optimization of the data generation process, it produces data that optimally challenges target models, leading to performance improvements of up to 13.2% in CS research tasks and 17.0% in legal reasoning tasks, while enhancing reasoning efficiency in mathematical problems.

hot.title: GPC: Large-Scale Generative Pretraining for Transferable Motor Control
hot.summary: GPC introduces a framework for transferable motor control by combining Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ) for discrete skill representation with a GPT-style autoregressive transformer. This system, trained on large motion datasets, generates diverse and naturalistic behaviors, achieving high tracking success rates and enabling robust recovery, while allowing efficient adaptation to new tasks through Conditional Low-rank Adaptation (CoLA).

hot.title: Rethinking quantum information in gravity and fields
hot.summary: A roadmap document from various Japanese institutions systematically articulates open problems at the intersection of quantum gravity and quantum information, categorizing them into four core themes to guide future interdisciplinary research and foster collaboration. The paper focuses on identifying critical gaps and promising directions rather than presenting new research findings.

hot.title: Parametric Skills
hot.summary: ParametricSkills introduces a framework that transforms free-form textual skills into model parameters (LoRA adapters) at inference time, addressing limitations of in-context learning for agentic LLMs. This approach enhances skill exploitation by overcoming instruction-following bottlenecks, enables context-free execution, and intrinsically links skill evolution with model learning, leading to improved performance in complex software engineering tasks.

hot.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Context Rot in Long-horizon Search
hot.summary: Xia et al. investigate "context rot," the degradation of LLM agent capabilities with increasing context length in multi-turn, multi-source deep search tasks. The study systematically diagnoses this phenomenon using a novel error taxonomy and evaluates various context management and rot-aware rejection sampling strategies, finding that a combined "Keep Latest with summarization" method provides an optimal balance for mitigation and significantly improves reliability.

hot.title: PhysisForcing: Physics Reinforced World Simulator for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: PhysisForcing, a framework developed by Peking University and NVIDIA, enhances the physical consistency of generated videos for robotic manipulation by reinforcing hierarchical physics supervision in interaction-critical regions. The method improved average success rates on RoboTwin 2.0 tasks from 68.2% to 72.8% and achieved a 9.2% performance gain on the R-Bench benchmark.

likes.title: DanceOPD: On-Policy Generative Field Distillation
likes.summary: DanceOPD is an on-policy generative field distillation framework that enables a single flow-matching model to effectively compose diverse capabilities like text-to-image generation and various image editing tasks. The framework consistently improves target capabilities, such as editing scores by up to 21.9% in specific categories, while preserving or enhancing anchor generation quality by up to 2.0% in T2I metrics.

likes.title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: OPID (On-Policy Skill Distillation) introduces a framework that enhances large language model (LLM) agents by extracting hierarchical, natural-language skills directly from their completed on-policy trajectories. This method consistently improves agent performance across embodied reasoning, web navigation, and search-based QA tasks, demonstrating up to a 26.5 point increase in success rate on WebShop for smaller LLMs and better sample efficiency compared to outcome-only reinforcement learning.

likes.title: Ask, Don't Judge: Binary Questions for Interpretable LLM Evaluation and Self-Improvement
likes.summary: The BINEVAL framework offers an interpretable approach to evaluating large language model outputs by decomposing quality assessment into atomic binary questions, providing fine-grained feedback and natural-language explanations. This method improved evaluation accuracy, achieving higher correlations with human judgments across summarization and dialogue tasks, and enabled iterative prompt optimization for both evaluators and generators.

likes.title: LA4VLA: Learning to Act without Seeing via Language-Action Pretraining
likes.summary: Researchers developed LA4VLA, a framework for pretraining robot manipulation policies by decoupling language-action learning from visual inputs. This approach, utilizing the LA-33K dataset of vision-agnostic action episodes, improves downstream task success rates, enhances robustness to visual perturbations, and strengthens language-action grounding in VLA models.

likes.title: Qwen-Image-2.0-RL Technical Report
likes.summary: The Qwen-Image-2.0-RL framework improves the Qwen-Image-2.0 diffusion model's visual quality and instruction-following by integrating reinforcement learning from human feedback and on-policy distillation. This approach achieved a +2.61 improvement on the Qwen-Image-Bench for text-to-image generation and a +78 Elo rating increase in human preference for text-to-image tasks.

likes.title: Qwen-Image-Agent: Bridging the Context Gap in Real-World Image Generation
likes.summary: The Qwen-Image-Agent, a training-free framework from the Alibaba Group, addresses the "Context Gap" in real-world image generation by actively constructing a comprehensive generation context from incomplete user input. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on the newly proposed IA-Bench benchmark, as well as WISE-Verified and MindBench, significantly improving upon direct generation models by integrating planning, reasoning, search, memory, and feedback capabilities.

likes.title: Previewing GPT‑5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
Introducing Claude Sonnet 5
Hallucination in World Models is Predictable and Preventable
likes.summary: Researchers at UC San Diego reframe hallucination in visual world models as a data coverage issue, developing three model-internal signals that predict hallucination with a robust negative Spearman correlation of approximately -0.80. Their work introduces the MMBench2 dataset and demonstrates that coverage-aware training and targeted data collection can prevent hallucination, improving downstream Model Predictive Control performance on unseen tasks by adapting models with as few as 50 trajectories.

likes.title: AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems
likes.summary: Kuaishou's AgentX is a multi-agent system designed for the self-iteration of industrial recommender systems, automating the entire algorithmic development lifecycle from idea generation to online A/B testing. Deployed in production, it increased single-worker concurrency by 8x and delivered a cumulative 0.561% gain in user app consumption time for the main feed, alongside over RMB 100 million in annualized revenue for life-service recommendations.

likes.summary: Researchers at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte developed Recurrent Generative Replay (REGEN), a framework enabling World Action Models (WAMs) to continually learn new robot manipulation tasks without storing original human demonstrations. This approach mitigates catastrophic forgetting, reducing Negative Backward Transfer (NBT) by over 50% in simulation and approximately 40% in real-world settings compared to naive sequential fine-tuning.

likes.title: Towards Automating Scientific Review with Google's Paper Assistant Tool
likes.summary: Google Research developed the Paper Assistant Tool (PAT), an agentic AI framework designed for in-depth scientific manuscript review, to address the escalating validation bottleneck in academic publishing. The tool demonstrated 89.7% error detection accuracy on a filtered benchmark of retracted math/CS papers and was rated by over 90% of authors as helpful in improving clarity and identifying substantive errors in pilot programs.
